name: Submersible Cavity Interdiction Drone SCID-2 'Lamprey'
description:
The SCID-2 is a narrow-profile autonomous drone designed to navigate fluid-filled or flooded infrastructure — drainage systems, cooling pipelines, flooded basements, sewage networks, and submerged tunnel sections. At 34 centimeters in length and 6 centimeters in diameter, the Lamprey moves through pipes and conduits inaccessible to conventional platforms. It is propelled by a peristaltic pump drive that mimics biological fluid movement, producing almost no acoustic signature and no visible wake in slow-moving water. Navigation is handled by a combination of sonar mapping and a pre-loaded infrastructure dataset that Helix Biosystems licenses from municipal engineering contractors.

The Lamprey's primary payload is a hydrostatic pressure charge — a compressed liquid charge that the drone positions against a target surface before detonating. In pipe environments, the blast is directional and catastrophic, capable of rupturing reinforced conduit or breaching basement walls from the waterside. In open flooded environments, the drone can operate as a guided mine, positioning itself beneath a target and detonating on proximity trigger. A secondary payload option replaces the hydrostatic charge with a neurochemical dispersal package, releasing a water-soluble incapacitant into a connected fluid system — a capability that regulatory bodies have flagged as a potential mass-casualty tool.

The Lamprey occupies a unique tactical niche in GLMZ because the city's infrastructure is extensively flooded and interconnected. The lower districts — particularly the Brackwater and Sump neighborhoods — sit atop a vast network of partially submerged tunnels and service corridors that Lamprey units navigate freely. Helix Biosystems markets the SCID-2 as an infrastructure inspection and repair platform with 'optional security configurations,' a framing that regulators have repeatedly challenged without success.
legality: Licensed (inspection) / Prohibited (armed neurochemical variant) / Restricted (hydrostatic variant)
specifications:
dimensions: 34cm length x 6cm diameter
mass: 1.8kg
propulsion: Peristaltic fluid pump, 8 chamber segments
maximum speed: 3.2 m/s in open water, 1.8 m/s in pipe flow
operational depth: Up to 40 meters
acoustic signature: Less than 28dB at 2 meters
payload capacity: 400g
standard payload: Hydrostatic pressure charge, 380g equivalent
alternate payload: Neurochemical dispersal capsule (regulated)
navigation dataset: Helix Biosystems Municipal Infrastructure License v4.2
battery life: 6 hours active navigation
communication: Low-frequency acoustic pulse, 400m range in water
tactical_use: Operators deploy Lampreys through storm drains, toilet connections, flooded access hatches, or any opening exceeding 7 centimeters in diameter. A pre-loaded target coordinate or manual guidance via acoustic pulse directs the drone to its destination. In offensive operations, it is used to breach walls from the unseen waterside, creating entry points or destroying infrastructure nodes. Defensive operators seed flooded tunnel networks with dormant Lampreys set to proximity triggers. The neurochemical variant, though prohibited, is reportedly used by certain factions to contaminate water supplies in targeted buildings — a slow-onset incapacitation method that is difficult to attribute.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's flooded lower districts, the Lamprey has become a symbol of the city's infrastructure being used as a weapon against its own residents. The Brackwater community has a tradition of 'pipe listening' — pressing ears to drainage pipes to detect the faint peristaltic hum of an approaching unit. Community defense networks have developed acoustic sensors from repurposed audio equipment to monitor local pipe networks. The fact that Helix Biosystems holds the municipal infrastructure data license — meaning their drones navigate the city more accurately than emergency services — is a point of significant political anger.
known_users: Helix Biosystems contracted infrastructure security teams
Brackwater territorial defense collectives (defensive proximity mine use)
Corporate sabotage units targeting rival facility infrastructure
A known smuggling operation using deactivated Lampreys as sealed waterproof cargo carriers
Municipal engineering contractors (inspection variant only, officially)
story_hooks: A Brackwater community leader hires the party to clear a section of drainage tunnels seeded with dormant Lampreys — someone wants the neighborhood flooded and trapped.
A Helix Biosystems engineer has gone missing after raising internal concerns about the neurochemical dispersal variant being sold through a front company.
The party's safehouse has a basement connection to the Sump network — at 3am, something peristaltic is moving through the pipes toward them.

Someone has been using Lampreys loaded with neurochemical payloads to contaminate the water supply of a specific residential tower — residents are presenting with unexplained neurological symptoms and no one is connecting the cause.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, biomimetic cylinder tapering slightly at both ends, resembling an eel or lamprey fish. The form factor is deliberately organic — smooth, hydrodynamic, purposefully evolved rather than engineered. At first glance, it reads as biological before the industrial details resolve.
physical_description.dimensions: 34 cm length × 6 cm diameter (roughly the size of a large flashlight or rolled newspaper)
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly dense for its compact profile — 1.8 kg feels substantial in hand despite the slim geometry. The weight is distributed evenly, creating a balanced, almost organic heft. Not unwieldy, but deliberate.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer shell with embedded pressure-resistant elastomer segments. The peristaltic pump chambers create visible ribbed segmentation along the body, like a biological organism's musculature.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with industrial-grade sealant. The surface has a subtle iridescent sheen where light catches the elastomer joints — faint greens and purples suggesting bioluminescent adaptation. Intentionally designed to fade into shadow.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey body with dark teal accent lines tracing the pump chambers. Translucent amber viewport at the nose cone reveals sonar optics. Minimal branding — intentional absence reads as regulation avoidance.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for human grip. Smooth, slightly tacky polymer that resists water. Mounting points are recessed and threaded for deployment apparatus, not hands. The body itself is grip-resistant by design.
distinctive_features: Nine visible peristaltic pump bulges running the length of the body, rippling visually like vertebrae
Translucent amber dome at the forward end housing sonar array and navigation optics
Recessed payload bay midship, seamlessly integrated into the hull
Micro-acoustic transducers embedded at the tail section, barely visible as hairline seams
Pressure relief vents along the lateral seams, designed to equalize without creating acoustic signature
Minimal exhaust ports — the drone produces virtually no visible discharge
Faint etching marks indicating pressure test ratings and depth certifications
Low-profile neutral buoyancy design — the drone neither floats nor sinks aggressively
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo etched in microscopic text along the forward 1/3 of the hull. Serial plate recessed beneath a rubberized access port at the tail. Regulatory certification stamps laser-marked in nearly invisible UV-reactive ink on the payload bay — designed to be present for inspections but invisible to casual observation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-deployed units show minimal wear — the smooth polymer resists corrosion and scarring. Sediment residue and algae biofilm accumulate on units left dormant in flooded systems, creating a living camouflage. Well-maintained black market variants are often cleaned meticulously. Military/faction units show micro-scratches from deployment apparatus contact and occasionally faint blast residue patterns where payload detonations have been survived.
